record.paper_title: Unsolved Problems in Visibility Graphs of Points, Segments and Polygons
record.original_question: Prove that there is a constant c such that every visibility graph of a point set with clique number omega(G) = 5 satisfies chi(G) <= c.

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Prove Conjecture 1 for visibility graphs with omega(G) = 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P$ be a finite set of points in the plane in general position (no three collinear). The point visibility graph $G=G(P)$ has vertex set $P$, with two points $p,q\in P$ joined by an edge if and only if the open line segment $pq$ contains no other point of $P$. Denote by $\chi(G)$ the chromatic number and by $\omega(G)$ the clique number of $G$.

Prove that there exists an absolute constant $c$ such that every point visibility graph $G$ with $\omega(G)=5$ satisfies $\chi(G)\le c$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general conjecture that χ(G) is bounded by a function of ω(G) for point visibility graphs remains open. Known results address only small cases: visibility graphs with ω(G) ≤ 3 are planar and 3-colourable, and ω(G) = 4 forces χ ≤ some constant (with examples showing χ can reach 6 while ω = 4). No source located resolves the ω(G) = 5 case, so its status appears to remain open, but this could not be definitively confirmed from the searched material.

status_evidence.title: On Colouring Point Visibility Graphs (arXiv:1610.00952)
status_evidence.snippet: Polynomial-time algorithm for 4-colorability; 5-colorability is NP-complete; example with χ=6 and ω=4. No statement resolving the ω=5 case.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work on point visibility graph colouring does not resolve the ω(G)=5 conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Colouring polygon visibility graphs and their generalizations
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion of χ vs ω for visibility graphs, with the χ-bounded-by-f(ω) question for point visibility graphs cited as open.
status_evidence.claim: Conjecture that χ is bounded by a function of ω in point visibility graphs is reported as open.
